absent: Child lookup and sibling ordering and parent linkage and identifier allocation for subsystem states beyond successor relations shown.
Full layouts and ownership and lifetime of group and subsystem and iterator and file context and worker and pool and work structures.
Complete permission model for delegation and namespace boundaries and domain membership and destination suitability.
Task resolution from input text and attachment mechanics and freeze and kill and type and statistics behaviors.
Workqueue flushing and coloring and activation ordering and pool selection and worker lifecycle beyond cancellation paths.
Timer and interrupt masking and atomic and list primitives owned elsewhere.
Build configuration effects on pressure files and debug variants beyond presence of conditional sections.

findings.text: Preorder and postorder and leftmost descendant helpers for subsystem state trees are visible outside their defining file for reuse by other traversal clients.
Synchronous cancellation and re-enabling helpers for work items are visible outside the workqueue file for use by other kernel components.
Enqueueing of work onto a dedicated kthread worker is available outside the kthread file as a shared service.

Preorder successor treats absent position as request for root and otherwise prefers descent toward children before ascending toward root in search of an unvisited sibling branch and ends when root is exhausted.
Leftmost descendant resolves to the deepest reachable node by repeatedly following child links until none remains.
Postorder successor treats absent position as request for the leftmost node under root and finishes after root and otherwise prefers sibling subtrees before parent.
Process listing is refused inside threaded subtrees while thread listing remains allowed and process mode uses combined iteration selectivity whereas thread mode uses empty selectivity.
Per-entry display emits the namespace-relative process identifier with line termination and reports success.
Write authorization is anchored at the nearest common ancestor of source and destination and additionally requires namespace visibility of both endpoints when delegation by namespace is enabled.
Attachment authorization layers destination suitability checks over common write permission and forbids whole-process moves that would cross domain boundaries.
Pending acquisition for work items retries internally until it can claim or steal the item so callers observe only settled outcomes without transient retry states.
Debug deactivation of work items has alternate build variants with delegation to a debug object facility in some builds and no action in others.
Bottom-half pool membership is reflected as an off-queue marker and pool reassignment during stealing preserves the pending indication.
Disable depth for work items saturates at its representable maximum with warning and symmetrically warns on decrement when already empty.
Subsystem tree traversal requires the caller to already hold either the cgroup mutex or read-side protection with assertion on entry.
Write permission evaluation against inodes and ancestor discovery require the cgroup mutex to be held by the caller.
Stealing or claiming a work item runs with local interrupts masked and additionally takes pool and read-side protection when inspecting queued state.
Active-count and in-flight accounting plus pending-queue activation require the owning pool lock with node-level activation adding a nested node lock.
Kthread worker enqueueing holds the worker lock across blocked-state checks and list insertion with waking only when idle and present.
Source group discovery during migration briefly holds dedicated spin protection with interrupts masked distinct from longer-lived cgroup and filesystem guards.

Core control table is an array of file descriptors each pairing a name with applicable callbacks for display and write and polling and release plus delegation or placement attributes and file offsets and closed by an empty terminator.
Pressure file table follows the same descriptor array pattern with per-resource file offsets and shared poll and release behavior and closed by an empty terminator and compiled conditionally.
Process and thread listing follows open with first-position initialization and sequential advance with position tracking and rewind by restart and release-time iterator teardown.

Migration by write progresses through live destination acquisition and task resolution from supplied text and source lookup and credential-scoped authorization and attachment with ordered cleanup and byte-count success reporting.

Deferred freeing of subsystem state distinguishes member versus self cases with release of counts and statistics first and then either member freeing with identifier removal or group teardown with parent reference release.
Synchronous cancellation moves from pending acquisition through disable marking and pool redirection to optional blocking flush and conditional re-enable.
Pending claim prefers timer removal for delayed items and then atomic claiming and then stealing from the owning queue with special handling for inactive items and linked barriers.
In-flight completion decrements active and in-flight counts and clears flush state when the last item of the flushing color completes and wakes the initial flusher when the final queue drains.
Active-count release for processor-local pools reactivates locally while unbound pools share a node count and round-robin through waiting queues when capacity frees.
Control file operations for process and thread membership expose start and advance and display and write and release hooks invoked by the sequence framework.
Deferred freeing runs as a work callback that recovers its enclosing subsystem state from the work container.
Cancellation warns when bottom-half work is canceled from hard interrupt context and otherwise requires sleepable context with early boot skipping the blocking flush phase.
Queue release cannot complete under pool lock and is therefore bounced to a dedicated worker to avoid self-deadlock.
Seeking in process listings replays from the beginning with a start position other than the beginning on first use treated as invalid.
Activating work across pools needs careful lock handover with retry when pools differ plus explicit kicking when the target differs from the caller.
Freeing assumes parent references keep ancestors alive until descendants complete and treats root reference expiry as a signal to destroy the whole hierarchy root.

Stable core control names are cgroup.type and cgroup.procs and cgroup.threads and cgroup.controllers and cgroup.subtree_control and cgroup.events and cgroup.max.descendants and cgroup.max.depth and cgroup.stat and cgroup.stat.local and cgroup.freeze and cgroup.kill and cpu.stat and cpu.stat.local.

Stable pressure names are io.pressure and memory.pressure and cpu.pressure and cgroup.pressure with irq.pressure present only when interrupt accounting is enabled and overall availability gated by pressure tracking support.
Control attributes include CFTYPE_NOT_ON_ROOT and also CFTYPE_NS_DELEGATABLE applied per file.
Failure reporting uses EOPNOTSUPP and EINVAL and ENODEV and ENOENT and ENOMEM for distinct conditions.
Iteration selectivity uses CSS_TASK_ITER_PROCS and CSS_TASK_ITER_THREADED to distinguish process aggregation from plain thread traversal.
Work state control uses WORK_STRUCT_PENDING and WORK_STRUCT_INACTIVE and WORK_OFFQ_BH and WORK_CANCEL_DISABLE and WORK_CANCEL_DELAYED for distinct conditions.
